clue.text: Excessively ingratiating, sergeant-major with host

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, especially an army

explanation.surface: A fawning soldier sucking up to a sergeant-major in front of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' here is the old sense of a large body of soldiers, not someone throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy describes oily, insincere flattery, someone ingratiating to an unpleasant degree.

clue.text: Old military governor using weapon heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means losing the heart, the central letter of the word

parts.note: a shotgun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A former army commander brandishing a gun without pity.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the seven-letter gun is its fourth letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary commander-in-chief who effectively ruled feudal Japan.

clue.text: A new suggestion over wine and appetisers

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A fresh recommendation for wine and starters at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just means the first pieces sit above the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters such as cured meats and olives, served before the main course.

clue.text: Head waiter, short man, tired out

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so drop the last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worn-out, small man in charge of the waiting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short man' looks like a description of the waiter's height; it means the word man docked of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maitre d' (maitre d'hotel) is the head waiter supervising a restaurant dining room.

clue.text: Dickens character, one after good wife in marriage

indicators.note: in tells us the trio of letters sits inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a match is a marriage or pairing

indicators.note: after places the letter for one behind the letters for good and wife

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a Dickens novel taking a second spouse, one following a good wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel Magwitch is the convict who turns out to be Pip's benefactor in Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Magwitch is the escaped convict in Great Expectations, one of the novelist's best-known figures.

clue.text: All do it wildly after a second noon drink

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second

indicators.note: wildly means in a disordered way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Everyone drinking wildly once just past midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium dry sherry, famously in Poe's tale The Cask of Amontillado.

clue.text: With complete licence

parts.note: arrant means complete or utter, as in arrant nonsense

explanation.surface: Given total freedom to act.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is a document granting authority, a licence to act.

clue.text: Lacking originality, solemn ceremony following end of feast

indicators.note: following places the ceremony word after that letter
end of means take the final letter of the word

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: A tired, formulaic ritual held after a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means hackneyed or overused, lacking freshness.

clue.text: Legacy of millions missing from retreat

indicators.note: missing from means the letter is absent from the word that follows

parts.note: a hermitage is a secluded retreat
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: An inheritance worth millions lost from a country retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from the past, an inheritance.

clue.text: Published by appropriate firm

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A book brought out by a suitable publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but it is the noun: a business.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is an informal word for a company or organisation.

clue.text: Messenger must save time for monarch's adviser

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it held, so the messenger's word holds the time letter inside

parts.note: a courier carries messages and parcels

explanation.surface: A royal messenger told to hurry and not waste time for the king's adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends at a royal court as companion or counsellor to the sovereign.

clue.text: Support me, being dizzy at the very top

indicators.note: dizzy suggests a spinning, jumbled state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A climber asking for a steadying hand because they feel faint at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest, in the topmost position.

clue.text: Jodrell Bank, say, excited boy over star

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A youngster thrilled at spotting a star through a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: Jodrell Bank is a famous radio telescope site in Cheshire, England; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodrell Bank is an example of an observatory, a site for studying the sky.

clue.text: Expert, notice, attached to English gym

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
PT, physical training, is school gym lessons

explanation.surface: A fitness expert's poster pinned up at an English gym.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the British school name for gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is a skilled person, a master of some craft.

clue.text: Hilarious team leaving

parts.note: a side is a sports team
splitting is slang for leaving or departing

explanation.surface: A comic scene of a whole team walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sidesplitting makes you laugh so hard your sides ache: extremely funny.

clue.text: Publican's current northern minder

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
a keeper is someone who minds or looks after

explanation.surface: A pub landlord's modern bodyguard from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, which is what an innkeeper does.

clue.text: Do well getting lead in Othello, or lead in The Tempest?

parts.note: to prosper is to do well

indicators.note: lead in means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An actor thriving after playing the lead in Othello, or perhaps in another Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead in' is used twice: first for a first letter, then for the starring role.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero, the exiled magician duke, is the central character of Shakespeare's late play.

clue.text: Religious belief concerning popular flower

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in means fashionable or popular
a carnation is a flower

explanation.surface: A faith centred on a much-loved bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation, rebirth of the soul in a new body, is a tenet of Hinduism and Buddhism.

clue.text: Intern beginning to cotton on okay

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: fine means okay or all right

explanation.surface: A trainee starting to grasp things and doing all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intern' looks like the noun, a trainee; it is the verb, to imprison.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, especially as a prisoner in wartime.

clue.text: Vague in court about former partner, American

indicators.note: about means around, so the words for in and court go round the other pieces

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An uncertain testimony in court concerning someone's American ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, not exact, hence vague.

clue.text: Mean swindle ending in tragedy

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle

indicators.note: ending in means take the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cruel con that ends badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means miserly, unwilling to spend, which is the tight-fisted sense of mean.

clue.text: Go round touring a European country

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the spinning word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to spin is to go round

explanation.surface: A tourist's plan to drive round a country in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a nation on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: First-rate cooking oil and mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the letter I for the digit 1

indicators.note: cooking suggests working things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Excellent cooking oil and mayonnaise from the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence.

clue.text: Reparation from that one mentioned

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone asking for compensation from the person just named.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run on from tHAT through ONE into MENTioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, which is what reparation means.

clue.text: Messaging symbol may show feeling about clubs

indicators.note: about means around, so the feeling word goes round the card-suit letter

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A text symbol that reveals how someone feels about nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoticon is a face built from keyboard characters, used in texts to convey mood.

clue.text: Cross, covering a mile in boat

indicators.note: covering means the bridging word goes over and around the other letters

parts.note: to span is to cross, as a bridge does

explanation.surface: An irritable sailor having rowed a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective angry; it is the verb, to bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Cartoon character, dressing, called out

indicators.note: called out means spoken aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the dressing

parts.note: olive oil is a salad dressing

explanation.surface: An animated figure in costume being shouted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests clothes, but it is salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive Oyl is Popeye's girlfriend in the long-running animated series.

clue.text: Society ultimately backing shop floor

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the letter is placed after the shop word

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so take the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A society finally supporting a shop's ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, a floor.
